ledger_source: Ballot: Silver Bulletin (Aug 24, 2026). Approval: cross-aggregator average of Ballotpedia, CNN, Decision Desk HQ, RCP, Silver Bulletin, NYT and others via Wikipedia (Aug 30, 2026).

headlines.headline: Trump's Approval Stuck at 33%, Democrats More Fired Up for Midterms
headlines.summary: Third straight Reuters/Ipsos poll at that level, with Democrats far more enthusiastic about voting than Republicans heading into November.

headlines.headline: The 2026 Midterms Are Coming Fast: Introducing CNN's 20/26 Vision Newsletter
headlines.summary: Launched a new weekly midterms newsletter the same week a CNN poll found Americans doubt Trump is paying enough attention to the country's most pressing problems. May sit behind CNN's metered paywall after a few free articles.

headlines.headline: Poll: Americans Sour on Trump's Washington Projects
headlines.summary: Post-Ipsos polling finds most Americans view Trump's high-profile Washington projects negatively, part of a wider pattern of underwater ratings across issues. Washington Post articles are typically paywalled beyond a free-article allowance.

headlines.headline: Trump Approval Rating Down 14 Points Among Republicans Since April 2025
headlines.summary: A UMass Amherst poll puts approval at 32%, with Trump's standing among his own 2024 voters and self-identified Republicans both eroding sharply.

headlines.headline: Republicans Get Senate Warning Sign From Four Fox News Polls
headlines.summary: Four Fox News battleground polls found Democratic Senate candidates ahead in Iowa, North Carolina, Georgia and Ohio, with voters more concerned about candidates' closeness to Trump than about Democrats being "too liberal."

podcasts.summary: September 1 episode asks whether Trump is inadvertently undermining his own party's midterm chances; recent episodes have also covered Susan Collins skipping a campaign stop with JD Vance and rising Democratic optimism about flipping Ohio.
Early-August episode covered a Senate committee voting to hold Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress and how Republicans are handling misconduct allegations against two of their own House members.

Late-August episodes covered Trump's border wall as part of a broader immigration-strategy reshape, and the previous week looked at whether moderate Democrats in states like North Carolina and Iowa point to a winning formula.

Mid-August episodes weren't midterms-specific: one covered Karoline Leavitt's departure as White House Press Secretary, another asked whether the Democratic Socialists of America movement is falling apart.

wildcard.label: Today's Wildcard
wildcard.summary: Trump's approval has now been flat at 33% across three consecutive Reuters/Ipsos releases — the flattest, most stubborn number of his second term so far.

note_from_this_trial_run: Second widened-net version. Podcasts went from 2 to 4 by switching to 'report what they covered, election-specific or not' rather than filtering for midterms-only content -- this is what surfaced Checks and Balance and The Rest Is Politics: US, both of which had nothing midterms-specific but plenty of real political coverage. The Bulwark, Inside Elections, Meet the Press, and The Daily still weren't checked in this manual pass (time-limited), not confirmed absent -- a real weekly run should check all 8. Headlines now carry the outlet's actual wording plus a paywall note where relevant, since links alone weren't proving useful when they dead-end at a paywall.
